questions.q: What is the hidden state of an RNN?
options: The input at the current step
A vector that stores what the network remembers so far
why: Correct: it is the memory that is passed from step to step.
The forecast is computed from the hidden state, but is not the same thing.

questions.q: Compute tanh(x·Wxh + h·Whh) with x = 1, Wxh = 0.5, h = 0, Whh = 0.9. Round to 2 decimals.
What causes the vanishing gradient in a plain RNN?
options: The error signal is multiplied by a number smaller than 1 at every step.
The learning rate is too high.
why: Correct: after many steps the signal is almost zero.
A high learning rate causes unstable training, not vanishing.
Missing values are a data issue.

questions.q: Which parts does an LSTM have that a plain RNN does not? Select all.
why: Yes, it decides how much memory to keep.
Yes, it decides how much memory to show.

questions.q: You need a quick model on one machine with little data. LSTM or GRU, and why?
options: GRU: fewer parameters and faster, often similar accuracy.
why: Correct reasoning for a first try. Always compare with a baseline.
RNNs can be used for forecasting.

questions.q: F = 3 inputs, H = 16. How many parameters in one GRU layer, 3·(F·H + H·H + H)?
Your LSTM forecast is no better than seasonal naive. What do you check first?
options: Check scaling, window length, leakage-free split and whether the baseline is strong for this data.
why: More size will not fix a setup problem.
Correct: setup problems and strong baselines are common reasons.
Without validation you cannot know anything.
